proofs.proof_tex:
For \(\alpha=(j,\omega)\in\Omega\), write
\[
 \mathsf{Succ}_{\alpha}(S,\ell,T,\tau)=1
\tag{1}
\]
when all of the following operational checks pass: \(S\in\Pi\); the source oracle returns \((h_S,\operatorname{supp}_S)\); \(\ell\) is a consistent catalogue label; \(\operatorname{supp}_S\{H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\}>0\); \(T\) is a single-district factor extracted from \(\operatorname{Slice}(S,\ell)\) with the measured-ancestry property; and \(\tau\) is a successful \(\operatorname{IDENTIFY}^{+}\) restriction transcript for the concrete assignment and equality type \(\omega\) of \(C_j\).  These are finite predicates by Definitions \(\mathrm{Legal\ protocol\ class}\), \(\mathrm{Measured\ source\ slice}\), and \(\mathrm{Restriction\ transcript}\).

The role of positivity in (1) is local.  If \(A\) is any event in the recorded coordinates of the acquired law, the slice handle represents
\[
 \operatorname{Slice}(S,\ell)(A)
 =\frac{\operatorname{Reg}(S)(A\cap H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell))}
        {\operatorname{Reg}(S)(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell))}.
\tag{2}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{Positive\ source\ law}\) makes exactly the denominator in (2) positive for a record actually used by a certificate.  No step below divides by the probability of an unused slice event, and no zero cell outside an asserted event is removed from the source law.  Measured ancestry is checked separately and does not follow from positivity.

Suppose that the explicitly specified complete run
\[
 \operatorname{CTFIDU}^{+}(G,Q,\mathcal R(E_0))
\]
accepts.  By Definition \(\mathrm{Structural\ target\mbox{-}factor\ tuple}\), its target factors are \(C_1,\ldots,C_k\).  By the construction of \(\Omega\), the complete finite branch loop contains every \(\alpha=(j,\omega)\in\Omega\).  For a fixed \(\alpha\), the source loop examines every decoded triple in \(\mathcal R(E_0)\).  Therefore acceptance implies
\[
 \forall\alpha\in\Omega\quad
 \exists(S_\alpha,\ell_\alpha,T_\alpha,\tau_\alpha)
 \text{ represented in }E_0:
 \mathsf{Succ}_\alpha(S_\alpha,\ell_\alpha,T_\alpha,\tau_\alpha)=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Indeed, if the existential in (3) failed for one branch, the exhaustive source loop for that branch would return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\), contradicting the assumed operational acceptance.

The two sets in (3) are finite, so choose the lexicographically first witness for every \(\alpha\).  Success and Proposition \(\mathrm{Connected\mbox{-}ancestor\ obstruction}\) imply
\[
 \mathfrak O(T_\alpha,C_j)=\varnothing.
\tag{4}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) then supplies a canonical successful transcript with at most \(|T_\alpha|\) strict restrictions.  Make one singleton-ownership record for each \(\alpha\), using its selected triple and canonical transcript.  The records own every branch exactly once, so there are exactly \(M=|\Omega|\), hence at most \(M\), nonempty records.  Their represented protocol set obeys
\[
 \operatorname{Prot}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})
 \subseteq \operatorname{Prot}(E_0).
\tag{5}
\]
Every record passes legality, literal typing, the one used-event positivity check (2), measured ancestry, source extraction, and transcript verification by (3).  Since \(c(a)\ge0\) by Assumption \(\mathrm{Binary\ rational\ cost}\), Definition \(\mathrm{Distinct\mbox{-}protocol\ cost}\) and (5) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})
 &=\sum_{S\in\operatorname{Prot}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})}\sum_{a\in S}c(a)\\
 &\le
 \sum_{S\in\operatorname{Prot}(E_0)}\sum_{a\in S}c(a)
 =\operatorname{Cost}(E_0).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]

For every \(\alpha\), its record contributes its successful triple to \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\).  Hence the complete source loop encounters a successful call at every concrete branch, and the complete run on \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\) does not return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  All other clauses of switching operational acceptance were checked above, so
\[
 \operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}(Q,E_{\mathrm{sw}};G)=1.
\tag{7}
\]

Conversely, if (7) holds, Definition \(\mathrm{Switching\ operational\ acceptance}\) expressly requires construction of the complete deduplicated source collection \(\mathcal R(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\), execution of the full unconditional procedure on it, and nonfailure of that run.  Thus the induced run accepts.  This proves precisely the operational equivalence
\[
 \forall\alpha\in\Omega\;\exists(S,\ell,T,\tau)
 \quad\mathsf{Succ}_\alpha(S,\ell,T,\tau)=1,
\tag{8}
\]
without replacing it by \(\exists(S,\ell,T,\tau)\forall\alpha\).  The proof establishes no semantic completeness extension of CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) beyond the acceptance predicate fixed in the core.

Operational feasibility means that some finite correctly typed acquired collection makes the specified complete run accept.  Theorem \(\mathrm{Switching\ source\ normal\ form}\) converts it to an accepted switching certificate without increasing cost.  Therefore the cover family in Theorem \(\mathrm{Switching\ weighted\mbox{-}cover\ frontier}\) is nonempty.  There are at most \(2^{|\mathcal A|}\) protocols and all weights are finite nonnegative binary rationals, so the finite minimum
\[
 W^*=\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,cup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega}
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S)
\tag{1}
\]
is attained.  The cover identity gives \(W^*=\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\).

For each branch, choose a successful witness from an optimal cover and split ownership into singleton records.  The normal-form proof verifies all record-local clauses and the full-run clause, so the resulting certificate is accepted and has cost \(W^*\).  The family of its canonical sparse encodings is finite: there are \(M\) branch indices; every protocol, label, and source mask has fixed finite width; and Lemma \(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) bounds each transcript.  Thus a lexicographically first minimum-cost member exists.  By definition it is \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}\).  The canonical certificate bound gives
\[
 N_{E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}}\le B_{\mathrm{sw}}.
\tag{2}
\]
The weighted-cover theorem's self-reduction returns this member and proves that each singleton owner needs only \(\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\) bits.  Its decoded fields are exactly the protocol, label, source, branch-index, and transcript outputs listed in the claim.

During incidence construction and self-reduction, cache the response under the \(|\mathcal A|\)-bit protocol mask.  Therefore a distinct protocol is queried at most once.  Definition \(\mathrm{Certificate\mbox{-}independent\ physical\ input}\) places every query and response bit in \(N_{\mathcal O}\).  Positivity is checked only for the event in each actually considered source slice, as equation (2) of the normal-form proof shows.  Nothing in (1)--(2) identifies a numerical value of \(Q\), and every appeal to CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) is to the operational acceptance test, which proves the final qualification.

Let
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\{E_{\mathrm{sw}}:\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}(Q,E_{\mathrm{sw}};G)=1\}.
\tag{1}
\]
If \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}\ne\varnothing\), Theorem \(\mathrm{Cost\mbox{-}optimal\ certificate\ feasibility}\) supplies \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}\) and
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star})<+\infty.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}=\varnothing\), Definition \(\mathrm{Main\ switching\ optimal\ acquisition\ cost}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}=inf\varnothing=+\infty.
\tag{3}
\]
The two cases are disjoint and exhaustive.

The cover identity proves
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:
 \bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \bigcup_{S\in\Pi}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega.
\tag{4}
\]
The last equivalence holds because \(\Pi\) is finite.  Theorem \(\mathrm{Switching\ source\ normal\ form}\) independently gives
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{sw}}\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists E_0\text{ finite and correctly typed such that }
 \operatorname{CTFIDU}^{+}(G,Q,\mathcal R(E_0))
 \text{ accepts}.
\tag{5}
\]
Negating (4)--(5) proves every infeasibility equivalence in the claim.

The incidence construction computes every \(K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\) and uses no more than \(2^{|\mathcal A|}\) cached oracle responses.  The exact dynamic program or protocol-subset enumeration tests (4) with the runtime proved in the weighted-cover theorem.  If (4) fails, the output is the uncovered-branch obstruction \(\Omega\setminus\bigcup_{S\in\Pi}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\), which is nonempty and directly checkable from the enumerated incidence table.  Positivity was queried only for candidate events used in forming that table; zeros in unused cells do not affect (4).  Since (5) is an equivalence between two executions of fixed algorithms, its negation makes no semantic completeness claim.

Fix \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}\in\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\).  For \(B\subseteq V\), the protocol
\[
 S_B=\{s\}\cup\{r_v:v\in B\}\cup\{\rho_v:v\in V\}
\tag{1}
\]
has exactly one fresh-unit SELECT, uses each mechanism at most once, is precedence closed and conflict free, and satisfies the stipulated ordinary physical compatibility.  Hence \(S_B\in\Pi\).  Independence and uniformity of its RAND coordinates give, for every \(b\in\mathfrak X_B\),
\[
 \Pr\{R_B=b\}=\prod_{v\in B}|\mathfrak X_v|^{-1}>0.
\tag{2}
\]
By the all-cells translation and the label-slice definition,
\[
 \operatorname{Slice}(S_B,\ell_{B,b})
 =P_b(V\setminus B)
 =Q[V\setminus B](\cdot;b).
\tag{3}
\]
Every vertex is READ, so measured ancestry holds.

Let \(\mathbf B\) be ordinary full-kernel identifying.  Equations (2)--(3) show that the acquired source collection is exactly the translated family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}\), for every intervention assignment and every outcome cell.  Lemma \(\mathrm{Single\mbox{-}world\ operational\ specialization}\) makes the complete translated run accept.  The switching normal form chooses one successful source for every branch; paid markers retain any acquired protocol not chosen by a branch.  SELECT and READ cost zero, so
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathbf B})
 &=\sum_{B\in\{B_1,\ldots,B_t\}_{\mathrm{distinct}}}
   \sum_{v\in B}c(r_v)\\
 &=\sum_{B\in\{B_1,\ldots,B_t\}_{\mathrm{distinct}}}
   \sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

Conversely, let \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}\) be accepted in the embedded catalogue, and put
\[
 B(S)=\{v:r_v\in S\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Adding missing zero-cost READ actions preserves SELECT cardinality, mechanism use, precedence, conflicts, physical compatibility, and cost.  Coalesce protocols having the same set (5).  It remains to show that every used slice is available from the complete ordinary family belonging to these sets.

Suppose a label fixes RAND coordinates \(D\subseteq B(S)\) at \(b_D\), leaves \(B(S)\setminus D\) unconditioned, and asserts a READ event \(R=r\).  For any recorded event \(A\), independence and uniformity of RAND labels give
\[
 \Pr_S(A\mid R_D=b_D,R=r)
 =
 \frac{
 \displaystyle\sum_{b_{B(S)\setminus D}}
 \left(\prod_{v\in B(S)\setminus D}|\mathfrak X_v|^{-1}\right)
 P_{(b_D,b_{B(S)\setminus D})}(A,R=r)}{
 \displaystyle\sum_{b_{B(S)\setminus D}}
 \left(\prod_{v\in B(S)\setminus D}|\mathfrak X_v|^{-1}\right)
 P_{(b_D,b_{B(S)\setminus D})}(R=r)}.
\tag{6}
\]
The denominator is positive exactly because the accepted record passes the positive-source-event check.  Equation (6) uses no positivity for an unasserted READ cell.  It expresses the used slice as a finite rational operation on the all-assignment members of \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B(E_{\mathrm{sw}})}\).  Marginal source factors extracted from that slice are therefore available from the same family.  Substituting (6) into each finite accepted branch computation, and applying the single-world specialization lemma, yields ordinary operational acceptance for every intervention-assignment and outcome cell of the full kernel.  Thus \(\mathbf B(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\) is ordinary full-kernel identifying in the stated operational sense.

With \(w(B)=\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v\), coalescing equal endpoint sets and the zero costs of SELECT and READ give
\[
 \sum_{B\in\mathbf B(E_{\mathrm{sw}})}w(B)
 \le
 \sum_{S\in\operatorname{Prot}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})}w(B(S))
 =\operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{sw}}).
\tag{7}
\]
The inequality may be strict when two READ masks have the same RAND endpoints.  If \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{ord}}\) is the ordinary optimum, (4) implies \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\le\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{ord}}\), while (7) implies the reverse inequality.  The same maps in the absence of a feasible design prove equality of feasibility status.

The published ordinary full-kernel hardness lemma applies to the finite-discrete, finite-rational class just used.  Equations (4) and (7) are a two-way cost-preserving reduction, so an exact or \(\rho\)-approximate algorithm on the embedded image would give one with no larger cost or approximation ratio for the ordinary problem.  NP-hardness and the \((1-o(1))\ln|V|\) threshold therefore transfer.  The structural map writes only the graph, catalogue, costs, and oracle signature in polynomial time; the ordinary law and support table remain oracle responses whose actually returned bits are charged by \(N_{\mathcal O}\).  This is the stated oracle representation convention.  The proof uses only SELECT--RAND--READ protocols and therefore supplies no action-cover approximation for catalogues with CTF-RAND, partial-child actions, precedence conflicts, or cross-action synergy.

added_lemmas.statement:
Put \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(M=|\Omega|\).  For the switching coverage sets and protocol weights,
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,
              \bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega}
       \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S),
 \qquad \min\varnothing=+\infty.
\]
The full incidence relation is computable with at most \(2^m\) distinct source-oracle queries and \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) work, and \(M\le k2^L\).  Branch-mask dynamic programming or protocol-subset enumeration, whichever is smaller, returns an exact optimum and a lexicographically first canonical singleton-ownership certificate in
\[
 2^{O(m+L+\min\{M,2^m\})}
 \operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})
\]
time.  A singleton owner is stored by one index using \(\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\) bits, so the ownership contribution for all branches is \(M\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\), not \(M^2\).  Weighted greedy returns an \(H_M=\sum_{r=1}^M r^{-1}\) approximation in \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) time whenever the instance is feasible.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For clarity, all claims in this proof concern the finite operational predicate \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}\).  They do not assert that this predicate is semantically complete on a larger model class.

We first prove the cover identity.  If \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}\) is accepted, take \(\mathcal P=\operatorname{Prot}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})\).  Every \(\alpha\in\Omega\) has one owner.  The owner supplies a successful quadruple \((S,\ell,T,\tau)\), so the definition of \(K_{\mathrm{sw}}\) gives \(\alpha\in K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\).  Hence
\[
 \bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega.
\tag{1}
\]
The distinct-protocol cost definition gives
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{sw}})=\sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S).
\tag{2}
\]
Taking an infimum over accepted certificates proves that the left side of the asserted identity is at least the cover minimum.

Conversely, let \(\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi\) satisfy (1).  For every branch \(\alpha\), choose the lexicographically first \(S_\alpha\in\mathcal P\) with \(\alpha\in K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S_\alpha)\), and then choose the lexicographically first witnessing \((\ell_\alpha,T_\alpha,\tau_\alpha)\).  Make one singleton-ownership record per branch.  By the definition of \(K_{\mathrm{sw}}\), every record passes all local checks, including positivity of its own event and measured ancestry.  The records partition \(\Omega\).  For every branch its successful source triple belongs to the decoded collection, so the exhaustive source loop encounters that success; hence the specified complete run does not return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\), and all clauses of \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}\) hold.  Deleting a protocol in \(\mathcal P\) that owns no selected branch cannot increase cost because \(w(S)\ge0\).  Thus the constructed certificate has cost at most \(\sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S)\).  Minimizing and combining with (2) proves
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,cup_{S\in\mathcal P}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega}
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S).
\tag{3}
\]
The family of protocols is finite and the costs are nonnegative binary rationals, so whenever the cover family is nonempty the minimum in (3) is attained.

We next enumerate the incidence relation.  There are \(2^m\) protocol masks.  Catalogue scans check SELECT cardinality, at-most-once mechanisms, precedence, conflicts, and allowed values; the published CTF-REALIZE runtime lemma checks physical compatibility in polynomial time.  Query \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}(S)\) once for each legal mask and cache the response, so at most \(2^m\) distinct queries are issued.  For each response enumerate the \(2^L\) labels.  Retain a label exactly when it is consistent and its asserted event has positive support.  This is precisely the denominator check in equation (2) of the normal-form proof; zero mass in an unused cell is irrelevant.  Each retained slice has at most \(|V|\) canonical single-district factors, and measured ancestry is a finite endpoint/fixed-value check.

For a factor branch whose free request positions have domain sizes \(q_1,\ldots,q_r\), the equality type is induced by its assignment and creates no further choice.  The literal table contains \(q_h\) distinct request literals for position \(h\).  Since \(q_h\le2^{q_h}\) for every positive integer \(q_h\),
\[
 |\Omega_j|=\prod_{h=1}^r q_h
 \le2^{\sum_{h=1}^r q_h}
 \le2^L,
 \qquad
 M=\sum_{j=1}^k|\Omega_j|\le k2^L.
\tag{4}
\]
For every surviving \((S,\ell,T,\alpha)\), construct the value-matching graph and execute the deterministic ancestor--district recursion.  Proposition \(\mathrm{Connected\mbox{-}ancestor\ obstruction}\) decides failure on its stated connected inputs, and Lemma \(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) supplies and verifies a canonical successful trace.  Thus all witnesses for \(K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\) are found.  Conversely, every witness in the definition is among the enumerated masks, factors, branches, and traces.  The enumeration is therefore exact.  Its number of local branch checks is at most
\[
 2^m2^L|V|M
 \le 2^{m+2L}|V|k,
\tag{5}
\]
and all oracle payload bits actually inspected are charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\).  Equations (4)--(5) prove the stated \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) incidence-construction bound.

List the legal protocols as \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\), where \(p\le2^m\).  One exact algorithm enumerates the \(2^p\) subsets and tests their unions.  A second uses branch masks: set \(D_0(\varnothing)=0\), \(D_0(U)=+\infty\) for nonempty \(U\subseteq\Omega\), and
\[
 D_i(U)=\min\{D_{i-1}(U),
 D_{i-1}(U\setminus K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S_i))+w(S_i)\}.
\tag{6}
\]
Induction on \(i\) proves that \(D_i(U)\) is the minimum cost of a subset of the first \(i\) protocols covering \(U\): an optimum either omits \(S_i\), giving the first term, or includes it, leaving \(U\setminus K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S_i)\), giving the second.  Thus \(D_p(\Omega)\) equals (3).  The two alternatives use respectively \(2^{O(p)}\) and \(2^{O(M)}p\) work after incidence construction.  Since \(p\le2^m\), choosing the smaller gives
\[
 2^{O(m+L+\min\{M,2^m\})}
 \operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O}).
\tag{7}
\]
Exact rational addition and comparison have polynomial bit cost because all action costs are binary rational.

The lexicographically first optimum is obtained by standard finite self-reduction, which we spell out.  Given a prefix of the canonical singleton-record encoding, force every completed record named by the prefix, reject intersecting ownership, subtract already owned branches, and charge every already used protocol once.  Recompute (6), or the protocol-subset alternative, on the remaining allowed witnesses and protocols.  The prefix has an optimum-cost completion exactly when this constrained optimum plus the forced cost equals (3).  Try the next bit values in lexicographic order and retain the first with an optimum completion.  The invariant that the retained prefix has such a completion holds initially by attainment and is preserved by the test.  At termination the certificate is optimal; an earlier optimum would contradict the choice at its first differing bit.  There are only \(M\) nonempty singleton records.  If
\[
 q_M=\left\lceil\log_2(M+1)\right\rceil,
\tag{8}
\]
the owner of each record is stored by its index in \(q_M\) bits, with index zero reserved for an empty marker.  Hence ownership uses \(Mq_M\) bits rather than \(M^2\).  The number of self-reduction calls is at most \(2^{O(L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) by (4) and the transcript-size lemma, so this factor is absorbed by (7).

Finally consider weighted greedy.  Starting with uncovered set \(R\), choose a protocol with nonempty gain \(g_S=|K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\cap R|\) minimizing \(w(S)/g_S\), and remove its newly covered branches.  Let \(W^*\) be (3).  If \(W^*=0\), some zero-cost cover exists and greedy always has a zero-ratio choice until completion, so its cost is zero.  Suppose \(W^*>0\).  For an optimum cover \(\mathcal P^*\),
\[
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P^*}|K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\cap R|\ge |R|,
 \qquad
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P^*}w(S)=W^*.
\tag{9}
\]
If every positive-gain member had ratio greater than \(W^*/|R|\), multiplying by its gain and summing would contradict (9).  Therefore greedy's ratio is at most \(W^*/|R|\).  Charge each newly covered branch that ratio.  Ordering branches by their cover time, the \(i\)-th covered branch is charged at most \(W^*/(M-i+1)\).  Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{Cost}(E_{\mathrm{greedy}})
 \le W^*\sum_{r=1}^M\frac1r
 =H_M\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}.
\tag{10}
\]
This is the explicit harmonic refinement, on the present protocol-to-branch cover, of the published weighted-greedy logarithmic guarantee.  Scanning all \(p\le2^m\) sets in at most \(M\) rounds is absorbed by the incidence-construction time in (5).  This is a protocol-cover guarantee; it does not assert an approximation for selecting individual actions under arbitrary protocol synergy.
added_lemmas.justification: The operational source-choice quantifiers induce an exact weighted set-cover problem on concrete branches, enabling both exact dynamic programming and a protocol-level harmonic approximation.
added_lemmas.gap: Dense certificate-string enumeration hides the much smaller choice between branch-mask states and subsets of legal protocols.
added_lemmas.consumer: A planner can enumerate physical protocol coverage once, compute an exact minimum acquisition, or use a certified \(H_M\)-approximation without treating individual actions as independent cover sets.

added_lemmas.statement: For the corrected finite all-cells translation of an ordinary full kernel \(Q[S_0]\), the complete unconditional CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) recursion on the translated family \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}\) accepts exactly when the ordinary single-world ID recursion accepts \(Q[S_0]\) from \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}\).  This is an equivalence of the two finite operational recursions; it is not a new semantic completeness theorem under event-local positivity.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Every member of \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B}\) is a single-world interventional kernel \(P_b(V\setminus B)\).  Under the all-cells translation, a labelled counterfactual term has one world label \(b\), so two copies never require a cross-world consistency or equality-type decision.  Counterfactual ancestor expansion therefore returns the ordinary ancestors in the mutilated graph, and the ancestral-set transformation retains exactly the same vertices and intervention labels as ordinary ID.

We prove equality of the recursion traces by induction on the size of the current source vertex set \(U\).  For the base case \(U=C\), both recursions return the same marginal of the same kernel.  For the induction step, the published IDENTIFY\({}^{+}\) recursion forms the least set \(H\), \(C\subseteq H\subseteq U\), closed against a parent-subscript value carried by a term outside \(H\).  With one world label, this is exactly the ordinary ancestor restriction for the intervention assignment \(b\).  If \(H=C\), both recursions return the corresponding marginal.  If \(H=U\ne C\), both return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  Otherwise both retain the unique bidirected district of \(G[H]\) containing \(C\).  The published recursion lemma states that the new source set is strictly smaller, so the induction hypothesis applies.  Thus every factor call has the same success or failure status.  The outer algorithms use the same ancestral districts and require every all-cells assignment branch to succeed, so their final acceptance decisions coincide.

No division by a source-cell probability occurs in this trace comparison: the inputs are symbolic full kernels.  When a later physical certificate chooses a conditioned slice, positivity is checked only for that used conditioning event before the recursion is invoked.

added_lemmas.statement: On finite-discrete semi-Markovian ADMGs with nonnegative finite-rational intervention costs and an all-cells full-kernel target \(Q[S_0]\), the ordinary minimum-cost intervention-design problem is NP-hard.  Under the standard set-cover threshold assumption used by the published reduction, no polynomial-time algorithm approximates it within \((1-o(1))\ln |V|\).  The reduction is cost preserving and its cover universe is represented by observed vertices.

source.locator: Theorem 2 and its set-cover reduction; the logarithmic threshold is the full-kernel hardness transfer required by the round-1 orchestrator directive
source.verbatim_statement: The ordinary full-kernel problem is NP-hard and its cost-preserving set-cover reduction transfers the standard \((1-o(1))\ln |V|\) polynomial-time inapproximability threshold.

attestation.note: The exact hardness content was supplied by the round-1 orchestrator directive; the immutable core identifies Akbari--Etesami--Kiyavash (2022), Theorem 2, as the ordinary NP-hardness carrier.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: If the independently specified oracle-instance \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}=(x_{\mathrm{str}},\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}})\) is operationally feasible, then the minimum defining \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}\) is attained by the lexicographically first canonical singleton-ownership switching certificate \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}\).  It outputs its distinct protocol masks, exact \(|\mathrm{LIT}|\)-bit slice labels, source masks, one \(\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil\)-bit branch index and one finite concrete restriction transcript per nonempty record, and it satisfies \(N_{E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}}\le B_{\mathrm{sw}}\) under the sparse canonical bound.  Each distinct protocol is queried once and cached, and every issued query bit and returned law-handle, support-index, and support-table bit is charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\).  The claim is exact optimization relative to \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\mathrm{sw}}\); it asserts neither a scalar identifying functional nor semantic completeness of CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) under the event-local positivity class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current claim bakes in obsolete exhaustive enumeration of \(B_{\mathrm{sw}}\)-bit strings and dense \(M\)-bit ownership masks.  The narrowed attainment statement retains the exact optimizer and auditable output, uses the sparse canonical branch-index representation, and leaves the strictly stronger weighted-cover runtime and approximation conclusions to the new frontier theorem.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Put \(m=|\mathcal A|\) and \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\).  Exactly one alternative holds for \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}\): either an optimal accepted certificate \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{\star}\) exists, or \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}=+\infty\).  The second alternative holds exactly when
\[
 \bigcup_{S\in\Pi}K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)\ne\Omega,
\]
equivalently when every switching certificate is rejected, and equivalently when no finite correctly typed generic acquired collection makes the specified full unconditional CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) run accept. This yields the exact identity \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{sw}}=\min_{\cup K_{\mathrm{sw}}(S)=\Omega}\sum_S w(S)\), an exact \(2^{O(m+L+\min\{M,2^m\})}\) optimizer, and a protocol-level \(H_M\)-approximation after at most \(2^m\) charged source-oracle queries. sampling_model.design: The structural input fixes the legal action catalogue and binary-rational costs and supplies a charged source oracle.  Each distinct protocol runs on fresh independent units, is queried once and cached, and may contribute any number of positive labelled slices to different concrete target branches without paying its action cost again.
sampling_model.units: Each SELECT draws one fresh unit independently from the target population, and the unit's potential responses are generated by one recursive finite-discrete SCM compatible with \(G\).
sampling_model.treatment: RAND actions replace the catalogued node mechanism for their affected children, while CTF-RAND actions deliver the specified counterfactual value only to their catalogued child subset; protocol legality also enforces precedence, conflicts, and at-most-once mechanism use.
sampling_model.overlap: For each record actually used, the exact support table must assign positive mass to its event \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\), making the displayed conditional-law denominator nonzero.  No positivity is imposed on an unused source cell or unused event, and measured ancestry remains a separate endpoint-or-fixed-value condition.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None is used.  The oracle returns an opaque complete-law handle and exact finite support; every query and response bit is charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\).  The results optimize operational acceptance and do not numerically evaluate a scalar identifying functional.
